title: Where Is It, in Which Frame: A Tree of Coordinate Frames and the Transform at the Right Time

questions.question: A laser sees an obstacle 1 m ahead of itself. What must be known to put it on the map?
options: Only the laser's range and bearing to the obstacle
The map's resolution and origin
The chain of frames from the laser up to the map, each a transform
The robot's speed at the time of the scan
questions.explanation: The laser on the base, the base in odom, odom in the map. The obstacle is known in the laser's frame. Each link up the tree turns it into the next frame's coordinates until it is in the map's.

questions.question: Halfway between headings of 170 and -170 degrees. What is it?
options: 180: the short way round, where averaging as plain numbers would give 0 and point the opposite way
0, the average of the two numbers
-170, the later of the two
90, a quarter turn from each
questions.explanation: 170 and -170 degrees are 20 degrees apart across the half turn. The blend takes the wrapped difference, so halfway is 180.

questions.question: How does a lookup relate two frames on different branches?
options: It cannot: only a frame and its own ancestor can be related
Via the nearest frame they both hang from, compose(inverse(target_from_common), source_from_common)
By adding the two frames' positions in the map
By going through the root every time, whatever the frames
questions.explanation: Both frames are worked out as seen from the nearest frame they share, and one is inverted. That is how a laser and an arm on the same base are related.

questions.question: A robot drives at 0.6 m/s and a scan stamped 0.5 s ago is placed with the latest transform. How far out is every obstacle?
options: 0.60 m, the speed for one second
0.05 m, one step of the lookup
Nothing: the scan's ranges do not depend on the robot's motion
0.30 m, speed times delay, in the direction of travel
questions.explanation: The scan was taken where the robot was half a second ago. Placed with where it is now, every obstacle is moved 0.6 times 0.5 metres along the direction of travel.

questions.question: A frame was reported until 1.0 s and a lookup asks about 1.5 s. What should happen?
options: Return the last report, which is the best that is known
Extend the motion at its last speed to 1.5 s
extrapolation: a refusal, since nobody measured the robot then and a guess would look like data
Return the identity, so that the caller can carry on
questions.explanation: Extending the last motion is a guess that would be handed on as if it were measured. The lookup says extrapolation and leaves the decision to the caller.

questions.question: What does a static frame mean?
options: It is the root of the tree and has no parent
It was reported once and may have moved since
It is reported at a lower rate than the others
It does not move relative to its parent, such as a sensor mount, and is known at every time
questions.explanation: A sensor bolted to the base is in the same place on the base at every time, so it can be looked up at any stamp.
